stories.title_en: Bleached corals thrive within days when touching healthy neighbour
stories.title_ja: 白化したサンゴは、健康な隣接個体に触れるだけで数日で元気に回復する

comments.author: skew-aberration
comments.text: Coral gets its color from algae called zooxanthellae, which it depends on for photosynthesis. Bleaching is actually due to the coral expelling those algae. Bleached corals are not dead, and remarkably they can not only let the algae in again but can also select a different algae species to cultivate (changing colour in the process)!. This is thought to be a deliberate survival strategy to optimize the species of algae under different conditions (Adaptive Bleaching Hypothesis). Bleaching is caused by the same stressors (like high temperature) which kill coral, but bleaching itself is not death of the coral.

comments.author: nomel
comments.text: > This incredible new result Only if you've never talked to anyone remotely involved with propagating coral, including those in the saltwater fish-tank community!

comments.author: ghastmaster
comments.text: Of note: This only occurred for fragments taken from an individual of the same genetic makeup(genet: basic meaning is they are a colony). I find it strange that the first observance of this was a year ago, especially given how rapidly it occurs. Coral bleaching has probably been studied since the 80s when major events started being noticed. If Stephen Palumbi is reading this, I would love to read why you think it took so long. edit: I would wager this is only the first published observance.

comments.author: anakaine
comments.text: Having been a diver on the Great Barrier Reef numerous times, the scale of bleaching events means that there is often no non-bleached neighbour for vast distances. Healthy propagation rarely occurs before the brown sludge sets in, then its game over.

comments.author: Okkef
comments.text: Only if they are clones - genetically identical. So not much use in practice, unfortunately.

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、 bleached coral が健康な隣接個体に触れることで短期間で回復できるという新発見の実際的意義である。コメントでは、この現象が遺伝的に同一のクローン（同じゲノタイプ）の間でしか観察されず、自然のサンゴ礁ではほぼ隣接した健康個体が存在しないため実用性が低いという指摘が多数を占めた。また、これまでの研究でなぜ今まで見逃されていたのか疑問を呈する声や、大規模な白化イベントでは健康な隣が見つからず「ブラウンスラッジ」が広がるため回復は期待できないという現場経験も共有された。賛否としては、発見そのものを興味深く評価する意見と、クローン限定ゆえに保全策への応用は期待薄だと疑う意見に分かれた。特に注目されたコメントは、グレートバリアリーフでのダイビング経験から、白化が広範囲に及ぶと健康な隣がほぼなくなり自然回復は困難だと実感を述べた点である。
stories.editor_note: 白化したサンゴが健康な隣接個体に触れるだけで数日で回復する現象は、微生物共生のメカニズムが解明されつつあり、日本のサンゴ礁保全にも応用可能だという点が注目されています。

stories.title_en: Dam removals are bringing fish back across the northeastern United States
stories.title_ja: アメリカ北東部のダム撤去が、魚の復帰をもたらしている

comments.author: goda90
comments.text: A rewilding organization bought some forest land, downstream from a dam, that used to get seasonal flooding before the dam was built and made an agreement with the dam operators to do artificial seasonal flooding via ditches they dug. The flooded forest has the effect of providing fish nurseries so hatchlings have a chance to hide and grow before the water recedes and they have to return to the river. https://youtu.be/qcVMX32c0io I think it's a testament that human activity and nature don't have to be all or nothing, but we need to consider and mitigate the impact of our actions and always leave space for nature.

comments.author: hinkley
comments.text: As the article alludes, the blueprint/precedent for this kind of work was set in the Klamath river basin in western Oregon. The local tribes deserve a tip of the hat for pushing through the lobbying and suits to get this process started. And a hat tip to all of the people who made the projects as successful as they have been in saving fish populations. IIRC, they ran into some surprises with volunteer fish which reduced the amount of hatchery fish they anticipated needing.

comments.author: glenstein
comments.text: More good news: after years of fighting, Brookfield Renewable agreed to sell four dams on the Kennebec River which will let Atlantic Salmon go back up river to their spawning territory. This just happened in 2025 and could be a bigger breakthrough than the massive alewife restoration that the article mentions. My understanding is that the first few victories on this were very very hard but it seems to have created a precedent and a growing example emulated across the country. https://themainemonitor.org/dams-sale-salmon-return-kennebec...

comments.author: twright
comments.text: This sounded familiar and then I realized I had read the same article a few weeks ago. This is some strange syndication I would propose changing the link to this one: https://biographic.com/death-by-a-thousand-dams/ it’s also way better layout and fewer ads.

comments.author: m_herrlich
comments.text: Good for the fish but as winters get warmer these dams will be useful to store rain that doesn't stay put in the mountains as winter snow. This might mean more summer droughts. Also a nice clean source of power. I would rather see fish ladders.

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、ダム撤去や運用変更によって魚の回復を促す取り組みの実例とその効果についてである。具体的には、ダム下流の森林に人工的な季節的氾濫を設けて魚の育ち場を確保する事例、クラマス川流域での先行部族主導の取り組み、そしてケネベック川での4基のダム売却による大西洋サーモンの遡上回復が挙げられ、これらは全国的に先例として波及している。賛否については、人工氾濫やダム撤去が魚類生息環境に良好である一方、冬季の降雪減少による貯水機能低下が夏の干ばつを招く懸念や、クリーン電源としてのダム利用価値、魚道設置という別解への関心が示された。特に洞察に富むコメントとして、人間の活動と自然を「すべてか無か」ではなく共存させる必要性を指摘した意見と、ケネベック川のダム売却が過去のアレワイフ回復以上のブレイクスルーになる可能性を強調した意見が注目された。
stories.editor_note: アメリカ北東部のダム撤去が魚の復帰をもたらしている事例は、河川生態系の回復が水資源管理に直結することを示し、日本のダム再評価論議にも影響を与えています。

stories.title_en: Furifont, a Japanese font that shows furigana
stories.title_ja: フリガナを表示する日本語フォント「Furifont」

comments.author: TazeTSchnitzel
comments.text: I think this is a rare “useful” abuse of font ligatures, and in that respect I think this is a cool project, but it's also a terrible idea that nobody should actually use, because Japanese kanji readings are famously ambiguous and context-dependent. The modal character has two different readings without counting those used in personal names, nor contextual slight changes to pronunciation. Some characters have six different readings, and that's again without counting those used in personal names. There's no way a font can do a good job at it unless you can somehow stuff an entire LLM in there. For context, it's a hard enough problem that Google Translate's own romanised pronunciation guides are frequently wrong, or disagree with their text-to-speech.

comments.author: shun_dev
comments.text: Really nice font! Native Japanese speaker here, and seeing furigana done purely in the font is very cool. One small thing on the Japanese version of the page: in the "Ligatures do the work" section, 合字 itself only gets じ over 字, and 合 has no reading. It should be ごうじ. I guess 合字 isn't in the dictionary, so it falls back to single kanji, and 合 is skipped because it has several readings.

comments.author: teshigahara
comments.text: Automatic furigana is not really possible to be reliable considering readings heavily rely on context that can't be easily inferred, but I'm sure it will help some people who can't read very well.

comments.author: jwolfe
comments.text: This is very cool. Unfortunate that it gives the wrong pronunciation when words get split in a line wrap (e.g., 大学 got split between lines and changed to incorrect furigana for me).

comments.author: alasano
comments.text: This is really nice. I'm able to read Hiragana and Katakana fully after about 4-6 weeks now but then I'm hit with the reality of how many Kanji I have to learn still everytime I want to read something in real life lol

stories.summary_ja:
**主な議論点**  
フォントのリガチュアを利用して自動的にふりがなを付けるFurifontの実用性。漢字の読みは文脈に大きく依存するため、フォントだけで正確に変換できるかが議論の中心となった。  

**賛否両論**  
賛成側は「フォント技術の巧妙なハック」「学習初心者にとって助けになる」「見た目がクール」と称賛。否定側は「漢字の読みは一字に複数あり、文脈が必要なのでフォントでは間違いが避けられない」「Google Translateのローマ字読みでも頻繁に誤りがある」「行端で単語が分割されると誤ったふりがなが出る」と指摘した。  

**注目コメント**  
- ネイティブ日本語話者が「合字」のふりがなが「じ」だけになっており正しくは「ごうじ」であると指摘し、辞書にない語はフォントが単漢字に fallback するため起こると説明。  
- 「フォントリガチュアの珍しい有用な悪用」と称しつつ、LLMを組み込まなければ正確でないとの見解。  
- 「大学」が行巻きで分断されると間違ったふりがなが出た例を挙げ、実用上の脆弱性を示す。
stories.editor_note: フリガナを表示する日本語フォント「Furifont」は、学習者や高齢者向けのアクセシビリティ向上に寄与し、Unicode対応の進展とともに国内教育現場での導入が期待されています。

stories.title_en: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017
stories.title_ja: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017

comments.text: DS isn't better than Sol and Gemini in the benchmarks, but after working with them all for a while now I'm beginning to understand why people find DS _feels_ so much better. First, it's the tok/s and TTFT from providers. Deepseek blazes through work - at quite good quality - and you don't find yourself waiting for your agents to finish. Second is the openness. comments.author: gregwebs
comments.text: The company's own news page: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news261017 They are showing this new version scoring significantly higher across multiple coding benchmarks, beating Sol 5.6 (6.1 is the latest) across 10/11 benchmarks. I am going back to DeepSeek for writing code. I was trying out using Sol and liking the result, but this should close a lot of that gap. I use Opus/Sol for an implementation plan and code review also use them for grilling. DeepSeek is also running verifications.

comments.author: AmazingTurtle
comments.text: so i did some apples to bananas comparison. i let 4 different agents review the same dirty code base (200+ files changed, c++, game engine): - deepseek v4.1 flash via deepseek API: took 20m to find one p1 issue that was relevant and a p2 issue that was irrelevant - glm 5.3 flash NVFP4 via TP2 DGX Sparks: took 1h 5m to find a p3 documentation issue - gpt 5.6 sol: took 5m30s for one p1 and one p2 issue. both relevant - gpt 6.1 sol: took 4m30s for two p1 and one p2 issue. both relevant. Worth to mention: none of those findings overlapped. I let deepseek v4.1 flash and gpt 6.1 sol both plan fixes for the summary of the findings. in this particular scenario: gpt 6.1 sol planned to increase a buffer size from 128 to 256 to fit the 191 elements that blew past a test scenario. it included some headroom. deepseek v4.1 flash on the other hand decided to make it exactly 191 to satisfy the test, for example. The TPS decode on deepseek is impressive. I never had a second / feeling of being left aone and though "damn this thing is working". Despite all my efforts, it took ~4x longer in a review, found less and planned worse than GPT 6.1 Sol. Wall clock time. I don't have token counts for comparison. If I were to grade those models from 1-10 (10 = top tier GG), I'd give deepseek a solid 6.5 and 6.1 sol a 7.5-8.0 maybe.

comments.author: pmxi
comments.text: Hilarious sentence: "DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks." (emphasis mine)

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、DeepSeek‑v4.1‑Flash‑1017の実用性とコストパフォーマンス、ベンチマーク結果と実際の使用感のギャップ、そしてオープンさや思考過程の可視化がユーザー体験に与える影響である。賛否両論として、ベンチマークではSolやGeminiに劣るものの、高速なトークン/秒と低レイテンシ、思考過程（CoT）の公開とレビュー制裁の不透明さがなく「感覚的に良い」という支持がある一方で、実際のコードレビューでは検出精度や修正計画がGPT‑6.1 Solに劣り、壁時計時間が4倍近くかかるという批判もある。注目コメントでは、DeepSeekのニュースページで複数のコーディングベンチマークでSol 5.6を上回ると主張されていることを挙げ、これがエコシステムの多様性を高めるべきだという意見や、バッファサイズをテストに合わせたExact値に設定するDeepSeekの保守的アプローチと、余裕を持たせるSolの対比が示された。要するに、速さと開放感は評価されるが、品質やタスク性能ではまだ先行モデルに及ばないという認識が共有されている。
stories.editor_note: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017は、推論速度と精度のバランスを極めたモデルで、日本企業のLLM活用におけるコスト削減と実用化の指標として注目されています。

stories.title_en: The Commodore 64 hardware simulator: break chips and pins, see the results
stories.title_ja: Commodore 64 ハードウェア シミュレータ：チップとピンを壊して結果を見る

comments.author: linker3000
comments.text: This is really cool, and a fantastic piece of work. It may come in handy when diagnosing / fixing C64 boards. Stretch goals: * Allow the simulation to run diagnostics carts. * On the 250407 board I have had timing edge cases with PLA replacements - the fix is often to fit a small (~100pF) capacitor on the /CASRAM line to slow it down a bit. The cap is fitted from the left leg of an existing 82 Ohm resistor and a nearby ground point close to 'RAM6'. Some boards actually have official space for the capacitor - designated C204. With some original PLA variants on real boards the capacitor may already be fitted. It would be good to be able to enable and disable this capacitor and set its value to see the effects. Write-up: https://linker3000.com/index.php/blog/poor64

comments.author: tombert
comments.text: I remember Byuu (RIP) wrote an article around ~10 years ago talking about why BSNES/Higan was "slow", explaining that it's really not slow given what it's trying to do. The more accurately you simulate the chips, there is simply more over overhead involved with synchronization and whatnot. I remember in that article they mentioned a Pong circuit simulation like this that was getting something along the lines of 10FPS of gameplay, which astonished me. You don't get a lot simpler of a game than Pong and even on amazing hardware it was still unplayable if you want the truest form of emulation.

I have been designing a cartridge in the back of my brain, and if this could assist before I start letting magic smoke out of my c64 it would be awesome.

stories.summary_ja: このシミュレータは実際のC64基板の故障診断や修理に役立つと高く評価され、特にPLAタイミング問題を解決するための/CASRAMラインに追加する約100pFのコンデンサをオン/オフできる機能や、診断カートリッジのシミュレーションを stretch goal として挙げられている。リンク先の書き込みではコンデンサの値を可変にして効果を観察できるようにする提案もあった。一方で、高精度エミュレーションは演算オーバーヘッドが大きく、Pongレベルでも10FPSしか出ず実時間動作は難しいという指摘があり、コードの最適化によるリアルタイム化への期待が示された。また、観測された動作から故障チップ・ピンを特定する逆方向の利用や、REUなどのカートリッジのメモリ転送動作を正確に再現できるかという質問も出ており、ハードウェア開発支援ツールとしての可能性が議論された。
stories.editor_note: Commodore 64 ハードウェア シミュレータは、レトロハードウェアの故障解析を可視化し、日本のハードウェアハッカー文化に新たな学習ツールを提供しています。

stories.title_en: Types of types: Haskell's Kind system
stories.title_ja: 型の型：HaskellのKindシステム

comments.author: adamddev1
comments.text: The more of Haskell's ideas that bleed into mainstream languages, the happier the world will become. It is just so beautiful how these higher abstractions can become so useful and powerful for tying all kinds of things together.

comments.author: cat-whisperer
comments.text: I really like the concept of dependent types, all type systems that I use rust or haskell have a very limited set of dependent types, but I do like the things that it let's you do

comments.author: i2talics
comments.text: I've long suspected that one of the things that makes monads notoriously difficult to explain to people outside of the Haskell ecosystem is that very few other languages even have a kind system that you are allowed to manipulate in code (and in some, like C++, it's so esoteric that you basically never see it). First explaining that you can even abstract over "type->type" kinded things gets you a lot of the way towards monads without actually describing monads.

comments.author: antonvs
comments.text: > These are the constructs we manipulate in our programs, things like 1, 2, True, "hello", etc… In functional programming contexts, they're also called "terms." This is not correct. Terms are syntactic expressions in a program. For example, 1+2 is a term, but it’s not a value. At runtime, it evaluates to 3. As such, some terms correspond directly to values - like 1 - but other terms represent computations that will be performed at runtime. tl;dr: terms are a syntactic concept, values are a runtime concept. Terms evaluate to values.

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、HaskellのKind（型の型）システムが他言語にどのように影響し得るか、そしてそれを用いた高階抽象（依存型やモナド）の説明のしやすさに焦点が当てられたことです。多くのコメントは、Haskellのアイデアが主流言語に取り入れられれば世界がより良くなるという楽観的見方を示し、特にKindをコードで操作できる点がモナドの理解を助けると指摘されました。一方で、RustやHaskellでも依存型のサポートは限定的であり、十分に表現力が高くないという懸念も示されました。意見が分かれたのは、Kindシステムが本当にモナド説明の鍵になるかという点で、一部は他の概念（例えば型クラス）も重要だと考えました。注目すべきコメントは、「Terms（項）は構文的概念でValues（値)は実行時概念」という区別を明確にし、1+2のような項が評価されて初めて値になるという説明で、型システムの基礎用語の混同を解く洞察を提供しました。
stories.editor_note: 型の型：HaskellのKindシステムは、型安全性の深化を示す学術的話題であり、関数型言語に関心のある日本のエンジニアにとって復習の機会となっています。

comments.author: cryptonector
comments.text: Fully software, even a combo of software and hardware, cannot by itself make elections secure. Think of the Reflections On Trusting Trust problem, the need to verify firmware, etc. You can't ensure that machines _will_ work correctly, but you _can_ verify that they _did_ . To do verify the machines' functioning after the fact you have to do it very soon after closing of the polls, and you have to devise a manual, statistical random sampling method where you manually check randomly sampled, marked paper ballots, against the digital cast vote record, then do a digital risk limiting audit to check that the CVR totals up to the machines' reported results. The sooner after closing of the polls you do this, the better the likelihood that any cheating will be caught. I.e., an immediate manual, partial audit of enough randomly-selected polling locations. That still leaves tons of other technical problems to address, like security of mail-ballots / absentee ballots, the security of ballot boxes used for early voting (because you probably cannot run the above manual partial audit due to then having nightly results available to the public; or maybe you accept that), voter registration, etc.

comments.author: glenngillen

Not entirely surprising, the duplicated build artifacts in each worktree being the main culprit here. There were some limited gains to be had by just being more efficient with how builds were managed but ultimately I just had to limit the number of concurrent features I was working on in a couple of particularly large repos. - more insidious was the fact I was actually hitting memory limits more than I realised and causing my mac to have to swap heavily. The system was surprisingly still quite performant while this was happening... until it wasn't. Unfortunately as best I can tell the only "fix" when this happens is to restart the machine. There's no way to have the system reclaim any of the swap space once it's written to disk. Which if you have it thrash a couple of times a day (especially easy if you leave something running overnight) adds up very quickly.

コメントでは、ESP32のファームウェアをWebAssemblyでブラウザ上でそのまま実行できる点が注目されました。これにより、実際のハードウェアが待たずにモバイルやバックエンド開発者がファームウェアを触れたり、CI/CDで実機相当のテストができるという利点が強調されました。また、同様のサービスであるWokwi.comとの違いや、ドキュメントの見やすさについても話題になりました。

**賛否両論**  
賛成意見は、「実際のファームウェアがブラウザで動く」ことの革新性と、開発フローへの適用可能性を称賛するものが多かったです。一方で、一部のユーザーはGitHubのドキュメントが過剰にフォーマットが濃く、読みにくいと指摘し、見直しを求める批判的な声もありました。

**注目コメント**  
特に目を引いたのは、自作のドローンシミュレーターでESP32のフライトコントローラーCコードをWebAssembly化し、ブラウザ上で実際のESP32と同じファームウェアを動かしている例を紹介したコメントです。これにより、シミュレーションではなく実機相当のコードをそのまま利用できる可能性が示され、開発者コミュニティから関心が集まりました。

comments.author: redsymbol
comments.text: To clarify something that the OpenCode team has done a bad job of clarifying: The leak was for something called 'OpenCode Console', which is distinct and separate from the OpenCode coding agent. If you're just using the coding agent, you're not affected. 'OpenCode Console' is a service that is similar to OpenRouter, but is much less widely used. The name 'OpenCode Console' is super confusing, because one might think it means the CLI coding agent. It does not. 'OpenCode Console' has nothing to do with the CLI/TUI coding agent, nor the desktop app version. The situation is made worse by the fact that 'OpenCode Console' barely has any documentation online, and the official leak announcement does not make the distinction clear at all. The OpenCode team did a terrible job of communicating this, and that's on them. Today is a bad day for people using 'OpenCode Console'. But most people, probably the vast majority of OpenCode users who are reading this, are not using 'OpenCode Console'.

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点：漏洩が「OpenCode Console」サービスのみに限定され、コーディングエージェントやCLI/TUIには影響しないという点が最も議論された。名前の混同とドキュメント不足により、多くユーザーが誤解し、チームの説明責任が問題になった。  
・賛否両論：一部はAPIキーの漏洩は深刻で、すぐに無効化できるエンドポイントが必要だと主張し、ホワイトハットや被害者側の対応を求める。一方で、実際に影響を受けたのはごく少数のOpenCode Zenユーザーであり、大多数は無関係なので過剰反応だと考える意見もある。  
・注目コメント：あるユーザーは「全てのAPIキーシステムにinvalidate_api_keyエンドポイントを設けるべき」と提案し、漏洩時の迅速対応の重要性を指摘した。また、記事作者は自身の投稿がHNのトップページに上がり、フラグされていることを嘆き、上 votes を呼びかけた。

comments.author: layoric
comments.text: Software is improving quickly so take these numbers as a snapshot performance at best. Strata has really shown how much performance is left on the table. I have a dual A4000 16gb (Ampere) on an old X99 dual Xeon E5-2680 v4 with 128gb of memory and Qwen 3.8 Flash Next at the IQ3-S size (~96Gb) runs at 65-75 t/s which is extremely useable.

comments.author: lopotubez
comments.text: I feel like these types of benchmarks mostly test what the mainstream tells you is possible and or works. You rarely get to hear the different implementations of inference engines, different types of setups (e.g. hybrid ones or older hardware) and their pros and cons. Also it seems these were tested with very minimal token usage. Currently on my 9 year old laptop with a GTX 1070 Max-Q 8GB vram, 16 gb ddr4 ram and i7 8750h. I am running a finetuned Qwen 3.5-35B-A3B (Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-GGUF-MTP) with 4-bit quant on a llamacpp fork (Turboquant) with 131k context at around 16-19 tk/s and 350-500 tk/s prefil using Pi harness. It is amazing for writing scripts and doing medium coding tasks and summarizing text for me. After around 100k context it goes down to 9 tk/s but that is to be expected. If you ever ask any frontier LLM or these types of benchmarks, they would probably say that the best model I can run on my system is a crappy 9B model or something, which is just completely false. So I really wonder how much more you can pull out from more powerful systems and much better open weight models.

comments.author: Jabdoa2
comments.text: By running vllm at work I learned that you will usually outperform benchmarks which you will find on the internet. Mostly by running proper parameter tuning. So you get impressive numbers. Still in reality those numbers do not tell the whole truth. We found that real usage is more 60k-140k prompt with a few k of output for realistic agentic coding workloads. Most of the time that will give you half to a third of decode throughput vs the benchmark. It also becomes much more about cache aware routing and kv cache management (how to offload and restore). Because prefilling 60-140k will simply take too long for interactive work.

comments.author: kgeist
comments.text: It says 46 tok/sec for Qwen3.6-27b 4 bit on RTX5090, but I get 60-70 tok/sec on a small context like that (5 bit weights with 8 bit KV cache), although it does slow down to 40 tok/sec on large contexts. If I add ngram speculation, then it can increase to 100+ tok/sec on code. There are many knobs to tweak to make it faster, which the site ignores.

comments.text: Prices for everything are all in flux at this moment. Consumer cards like RTX 5090 are bonkers. Even 3090s have like doubled in the last six months. Meanwhile, prices for renting this class of hardware on vast.ai are spiking too, with rates increasing like 50% in September alone. It's hard to know if we're at the beginning or the end of this trend. If manufacturing continues to focus on high end datacenter gpus at $40k a pop, and we continue to have supply constraints, this could last a while. On the other hand, if Chinese models continue to nip at the tails of the frontier, cheaper by 20x, running on new Chinese chips, the whole bottom could fall out of the US market, and things could get very weird.

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、ローカルLLMの実際スループットがベンチマークと乖離しやすいこと、ソフトウェア最適化や量子化、KVキャッシュ管理などのチューニングで性能を大きく伸ばせる点、そしてGPU価格の高騰と供給不安が導入コストに与える影響。賛否は、ベンチマーク数値はあくまで目安であり実務ではコンテキスト長増大でデコード速度が半分以下になるという懐疑的意見と、ngramスペキュレーションや適切なパラメータチューニングで理論値を上回れるという楽観的意見に分かれた。注目コメントとして、9年前のGTX 1070 Max‑Qでも4bit量子化したQwen 3.5‑35Bを131kコンテキストで16‑19tok/s程度で動かし、スクリプト作成や中規模コーディングに実用的であると指摘した意見が挙げられ、ハードウェアだけでなくソフトウェア側の工夫が性能を左右するという洞察が示された。

comments.author: ogoffart
comments.text: I have noticed the same on my project. The agent helps a lot to fix bugs. Just point the agents at the bug reports. They do the reproduction, debugging and fixes. We "just" have to review. (Sometimes ask more details and tell we'd prefer another approach.) This makes bug fixing much faster and automated. And at the same time, it seems we get less bug reports to our library. I think user just use their agents to code, and agents don't report bugs, they just work it around somehow. So overall, the open bug count is decreasing. Which somehow feels good. On the other hand, we get a lot of PR made by other's people agents, which can be a bit overwhelming when it's just a huge code drop. We can't easily review that.
